	fi

# THE EDIT LOOP: the source built by the STANDING compiler into
# build/avra-try, never over it — so the builder's print, and every row its
# store holds, stands from one edit to the next. `./avra-try` runs it. A
# change the compiler must READ to build itself (codegen, the front end, a
# refusal about its own source) reaches the product only through `make avra`.
try: $(COMPILER_OBJS)
	@sh tools/capped.sh build/avra-try-build.out 200000 env AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release ./avra build packages/cli --time || { cat build/avra-try-build.out; exit 1; }
	@grep '^time: ast' build/avra-try-build.out | grep -oE 'held [0-9]+/[0-9]+' || true
	@cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra-try.next && mv -f build/avra-try.next build/avra-try
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra-try 2>/dev/null || true
	@rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
	@echo "try: build/avra-try — ./avra-try runs it"

# THE WARM EDIT LOOP, measured: a one-edit check and build of the cli, and `make try` on a leaf and a core edit.
edit-loop:
	@sh tools/db_measure/edit_loop.sh

# THE INSTALL: the binary under bin/, and what it finds from its own
# directory — the runtime's object and every std package — under
# lib/avra/. A program anywhere then says `use @std.io` with no
# manifest row, and links.
PREFIX ?= /usr/local
install: avra
	@mkdir -p $(PREFIX)/bin $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/std

# inside all of them.

export fn generator_run(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    l: Lowered,
    g: GeneratorAt,
    file: SourceFileAddress,
    name: string,
    handed: List<HandedArg>,
    budgets: Budgets,
    plan: EvalPlan? = null,
    method: MethodSite? = null,
) -> GeneratorRun {
    let values = handed_values(engine, file, name, g.kind.first_seat(), handed, method)
    if !values.stopped.is_empty() { return GeneratorRun.Stopped(values.stopped, values.fault, values.said) }

        l,
        generator_symbol(g),
        values.args,
        values.heap,
        budgets,
        (n: string) -> named_lifted(engine, file, n),

        plan,
        late: late_door(task_survey(engine), TaskChecks.Tested),
    ) {
        .Ok(lifted) -> match answer_shape(engine, g) {
            .Declared -> GeneratorRun.Ran(lifted.declared_made(), lifted.declared_problems()),
            .Directives -> GeneratorRun.Ran(lifted.directives(), []),
            .Diagnostics -> GeneratorRun.Ran([], lifted.saids()),
            .Nothing -> GeneratorRun.Ran([], []),
        },
        .Err(why) -> GeneratorRun.Trapped(unsettled_label(annotation_named(g), why)),
    }
}

/// What the statement `s` writes as the fn `name`, a declared fn's or an extern's; absent for any
/// other statement.
fn written_at(store: SyntaxArena, s: StmtId, name: string) -> WrittenFn? {
    let declared? = store.fn_parts(s) else {
        let external? = store.extern_parts(s) else { return null }
        if external.name != name { return null }
        return WrittenFn {
            type_params: [],
            params: external.params,
            ret: external.ret,
            writer: written_by(store, s),
        }

    if declared.name != name { return null }

        defaults: [t.type_default for t in declared.tparams],
        params: declared.params,
        ret: declared.ret,
        writer: written_by(store, s),
    }
}

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 18 20:17:24 2026 +0000

    ctx, step 1: declare, set and read; the frame on the task, back at a block's end and a caught trap
    
    `ctx name: T = v` declares a context at a module's top level, `ctx name = v` sets it for the rest of
    its block, and `ctx.name` reads it: what the nearest set still in force gave it, else its default,
    kept once as a module `state`'s start is. A set ends as its scope does, by every way out of it; a
    caught trap puts back the frame its guard was entered under, in both engines. A context is new-only:
    the old path refuses each form, and the net sets it aside. A context is named and imported as any
    top-level name; its key is a number of its declared symbol, so a library's context wears one key in
    every program that links it. `ctx` is a soft keyword: a binding of that name stays ordinary, but
    `ctx.name` always reads a context, so the soundness walk's own `ctx` is `facts`.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

impl AppliedScope {
    /// The type `t` and each it holds, where applied to what it doesn't take, outermost first.
    fn misapplied(t: TypeRef) -> List<List<string>> {
        let own = if t.arrow { [] } else { self.own_misapplied(t) }
        own.concat(flatten([self.misapplied(a) for a in t.type_args().concat(t.alternatives)]))
    }

    /// The type `t` itself applied to what it doesn't take; nothing for a name that names no type
    /// this law knows the parameters of.
    fn own_misapplied(t: TypeRef) -> List<List<string>> {
        let name = t.name
        if name.is_empty() || name == INFERRED || name == self_word || self.params.contains(name) { return [] }
        let takes? = self.takes(name) else { return [] }
        let found = t.applied.length
        if takes == 0 && found > 0 { return [["none", name]] }
        if fills(takes, self.spared(name), found) { return self.keyed_words(t) }
        if found == 0 { return [["bare", name, "${takes}"]] }

// The AST source projection: its output parses, reaches a fixed point
// after one projection, and keeps the structure readers depend on.

use @std.avrac.testing.{projected}

fn stable(source: string) -> bool {
    let out = projected(source)
    out != "<parse refused>" && projected(out) == out && same_tree(source, out)
}

fn same_tree(source: string, projected: string) -> bool {
    let before = parse_source(source)
    let after = parse_source(projected)
    if !before.voices.list.is_empty() ||
        !after.voices.list.is_empty() ||
        before.stmts.length != after.stmts.length {
        return false
    }
    for j, stmt in before.stmts {
        if before.store.stmt_fingerprint(stmt) != after.store.stmt_fingerprint(after.stmts[j]) { return false }
    }
    true
}

/// `l == r` over values of a type the language owns, each side kept: both sides' registers and
/// whether they are one value; absent where the sides aren't of such a type.
export type SidesCompared = { left: Reg, right: Reg, same: Reg }

/// `l == r` lowered with both sides kept, where both are of one type the language owns.
export fn sides_compared(mut cx: Lowering, l: ExprId, r: ExprId) -> SidesCompared? {
    let kind? = operands(cx, l, r) else { return null }
    let a = cx.lower(l)
    let b = cx.lower(r)
    SidesCompared { left: a, right: b, same: owned_same(cx, kind, a, b) }
}

/// Whether two values of a type the language owns, of the operand kind `kind`, are one value.
fn owned_same(mut cx: Lowering, kind: Operand, a: Reg, b: Reg) -> Reg {
    match kind {
        .Text -> cx.call_row(Layout.Truth, rt_sig_of("avra_streq")!, [a, b]),
        .Octets -> cx.call_row(Layout.Truth, rt_sig_of("avra_bytes_eq")!, [a, b]),
        .Number or .Truth -> cx.bin(Layout.Truth, BinOp.Eq, a, b),
    }
}

//! A SQLite refusal as a home's: which of a home's errors each cause is.
use @std.queue.{HomeError}
use @std.sqlite.error.{Cause, SqlError}
use @std.time.{Duration, ms}

/// How long a sender waits before it asks a busy or full home again.
export const ask_again: Duration = ms(250)

/// A store answer as a home's.
export fn homed<V>(r: Result<V, SqlError>) -> Result<V, HomeError> {
    match r { .Ok(v) -> .Ok(v), .Err(e) -> .Err(home_error(e)) }
}

/// A lock another connection holds is waited out and asked again; a
/// database the caller may not write is a denial; every other cause is
/// a refusal in SQLite's own words.
export fn home_error(e: SqlError) -> HomeError {
    match e.cause {
        .Busy(_) or .Interrupted -> HomeError.Unreachable(ask_again),
        .Denied(_) -> HomeError.Denied,
        .Constraint(_) or .Mismatch(_, _, _) or .NoColumn(_) or .OutOfRow(_, _) or .OutOfSlots(_, _) or .Unfilled(_, _) or .NotUtf8(_, _) or .NoRow or .ManyRows or .Syntax or .Corrupt or .Full or .TooBig or .Io(_) or .NoMemory or .CantOpen or .NotADatabase or .Expired or .Defect(_) or .Other(_) or .EmptyPath or .UriPath or .HoldsNul or .ManyStatements or .NoStatement or .RowsDiscarded or .Finalized or .Done or .Closed or .Foreign or .NoTransaction or .TransactionOpen or .NegativeWait or .Unlogged -> HomeError.Refused(e.message),
    }
}

    }
}

    let at? = match seat {

    } else { return null }
    let label? = store.means_note(at) else { return null }
    SugarNote { label: label, at: kept_at(store.expr_span(at)) }
}

/// Each body the written item `at` of `file` declares, signed and typed as its query keeps it: each
/// fn's, then each method's and static's an impl there writes that declares no type parameters of
/// its own.
fn item_signed_bodies(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int, item: ReadItem) -> List<
    CheckedBody,
> {
    let fns = [CheckedBody { signed: b!, typed: typed_fn(engine, file, p!.name)! } for s in item.stmts for p in [item.store.fn_parts(s)] if p != null for b in [signed_body(engine, file, p!.name)] if b != null]
    fns
        .concat(
            [CheckedBody { signed: m!.signed, typed: method_body_typed(engine, a, name, statics) } for a in impls_at(engine, file, at) for s in impl_fns(item, a) if item.store.fn_parts(s)!.tparams.is_empty() for name in [item.store.fn_parts(s)!.name] for statics in [item.store.is_static(s)] for m in [signed_method(engine, a, name, statics)] if m != null],
        )
}

/// A body an item declares, signed, beside its typing.
type CheckedBody = { signed: SignedBody, typed: TypedBody }

/// Each method call in the body `b` that its type parameter's bound doesn't give.
fn body_ungiven(engine: QueryEngine, text: string, b: CheckedBody) -> List<UngivenAt> {
    let signed = b.signed
    let typed = b.typed
    let store = signed.item.store
    let own = [p.name.of for p in store.fn_parts(signed.stmt)?.tparams ?? []]
    [r! for k in 0..typed.types.length if called_on(store, ExprId { index: k }) != null for r in [ungiven(engine, store, text, signed.signature, own, typed.types, ExprId { index: k })] if r != null]
}

/// `if … != null { v }`, since a type name and a value name share
/// one lexical class. Entries keep written order, which is the
/// spread's precedence.
///
/// STAYS A FUNCTION: entries are ordered by source offset across keys, values and spreads.
@computed
fn struct_lit_written(s: dyn Slots) -> Result<Built, string> {
    let store = s.arena()
    let spans = s.spans_of("keys")?
    let keys = [Key { text: t, at: spans[j]! } for j, t in s.texts_of("keys")?]
    let vals = s.exprs_of("vals")?
    let dots = flatten([some_list(d) for d in s.spans_of("dots")?])
    let written = [value_after(store, keys, vals, j) for j, _k in keys]
    if [v for v in written if v != null].length != vals.length { return .Err(zip_defect) }
    let named = [Written {
        at: keys[j].at.lo,
        name: if dots.any(spreads_onto(it, keys[j].at, keys)) { "..${keys[j].text}" } else { keys[j].text },
        value: v ?? store.alloc_expr(Expr.Ident(Scoped(keys[j].text)), s.built_at()),
    } for j, v in written]
    let whole = [Written { at: store.expr_span(w)?.lo ?? 0, name: spread_entry, value: w } for w in s.exprs_of("whole")?]
    let entries = sorted_by(named.concat(whole), (x, y) -> x.at < y.at)
    let lit = store
        .alloc_expr(
            Expr
                .StructLit(
                    Nominal(s.text_of("name")?),
                    [Plain(x.name) for x in entries],
                    [x.value for x in entries],
                ),
            s.built_at(),
        )
    store.mark_struct_targs(lit, s.types_of("targs")?)
    .Ok(Built.Expr(lit))
}

/// A Var the arguments leave free is pinned by the ANSWER's seat: the
/// declared return unifies with the want the seat planted (`let xs:
/// List<int> = empty()`, `Store { exprs: new_arena() }`, an argument
/// seat, a fn's declared answer). With no want yet the call goes
/// HUNGRY, like a generic literal, and speaks only when the walk ends
/// starving.
fn pinned_by_answer(cx: TypeCx, e: ExprId, ret: TypeId, decl: DeclId, mut bound: Pins) {
    let wanted? = cx.want_at(e) else { return }
    if cx.unify(ret, wanted, decl, bound) || cx.view.types.carried(ret) != null { return }
    let present? = cx.view.types.carried(wanted) else { return }
    let _ = cx.unify(ret, present, decl, bound)
}

/// `x.m<T>(a)` — the call, its written type arguments kept beside it in the store.
@computed
fn method_pinned_written(s: dyn Slots) -> Result<Built, string> {
    let store = s.arena()
    let call = store

            Expr.MethodCall(s.expr_of("subject")?, Plain(s.text_of("name")?), s.exprs_of("args")?),

//! What a `for` loop means, in the core.
use core.{At, Stmt, SyntaxArena}
use features.{TypedCode, meaning}

/// `for x in xs { … }` over a list walks its positions up to its length, read once — a text's `chars`
/// view, which is no list until one is asked for, is walked by the statement's own rule; `for i in
/// lo..hi { … }` counts from `lo` up to `hi`, each read once. Each turn binds the element or the count, and
/// counts past it before the body runs, so a `continue` never turns forever.
export meaning for_each {
    quote { for ${x} in ${xs} { ${..body} } } if walks_a_list(xs) && !views_chars(xs) && !breaks_by_label(body) -> quote {
        let items = ${xs}
        let count = items.length
        mut at = 0
        while at < count {
            let ${x} = items[at]
            at = at + 1
            ${body}
        }
    },
    quote { for ${i} in ${lo}..${hi} { ${..body} } } if !breaks_by_label(body) -> quote {
        mut at = ${lo}
        let end = ${hi}
        while at < end {
            let ${i} = at
            at = at + 1
            ${body}
        }
    },
}

/// Whether the subject is a list, as typing found it.
fn walks_a_list(xs: TypedCode) -> bool { xs.type()?.listed() != null }

/// Whether the subject is a `chars()` view.
fn views_chars(xs: TypedCode) -> bool {
    match xs.at {
        .Expr(e) -> match xs.of.view.store.expr(e) {
            .MethodCall(_, name, args) -> name.of == "chars" && args.is_empty(),
            rest -> false,
        },
        rest -> false,
    }
}

/// Whether any statement of the body leaves a loop by a label, which names the loop itself.

//! `meaning` — what a sugar means, written in the language it means:
//! `meaning coalesce { quote { ${a} ?? ${b} } -> quote { match ${a} { v? -> v, null -> ${b} } } }`
//! is an instance of `component meaning` below, its arms filling `run` as a `rule`'s do (the arms
//! sugar's `_ -> null` tail included). The subject is `it`, one node of an item typing has read; a
//! pattern's holes bind nodes of that item, and a template splices each back as the node it is,
//! never as its text, so its span, its type and its own meaning come with it.
use core.{At, SignedType, SyntaxArena}
use @std.meta.{Node, Rewrite}

/// An item's syntax, where a quote pattern reads it.
export type TypedView = { store: SyntaxArena }

/// What a meaning reads of the item it rewrites: its syntax, and each expression's type as typing
/// found it.
export type TypedItem = { view: TypedView, types: List<SignedType?> }

/// One node of a typed item: the subject a meaning matches, and what its pattern's holes bind.
export type TypedCode = { of: TypedItem, at: At }

impl TypedCode {
    /// The type typing found for this node, absent for a node that isn't an expression or wasn't
    /// typed.
    fn type() -> SignedType? {
        match self.at {
            .Expr(id) -> if id.index < self.of.types.length { self.of.types[id.index] } else { null },
            .Stmt(_) or .Pat(_) or .Field(_, _) or .Param(_, _) -> null,
        }
    }
}

/// A handle on each of `ats`, in `of`: what a run hole binds.
export fn
…[378 chars cut]…
at(id) -> held_node("pat", id.index),
        .Stmt(id) -> held_node("stmt", id.index),
        .Field(_, _) or .Param(_, _) -> held_node("none", 0),
    }
}

/// The nodes a run of handles holds, as one fill.
export fn typed_codes_node(ms: List<TypedCode>) -> Node { Node.Many([typed_code_node(m) for m in ms]) }

/// A node of the arena as a fill: its arena's word and its index.
fn held_node(arena: string, index: int) -> Node { Node.Many([Node.Name(arena), Node.Int(index)]) }

export component meaning {
    run: fn(TypedCode) -> Rewrite?
    doc: string = ""
}

/// The literal `lit` at `e`, writing the leading type arguments `written`, refused where it leaves the
/// parameter `open` of `record` pinned by nothing: named by the fields it leaves unwritten that could.
fn unpinned_literal(
    mut cx: Checking,
    e: ExprId,
    lit: StructLit,
    record: RecordShape,
    open: int,
    written: List<TypeRef>,
) {
    let unwritten = [f.name for f in record.fields if !lit.fields.any(it.of == f.name) && (f.ty?.parameters() ?? []).contains(open)]
    let param = if open < record.names.length { record.names[open] } else { "${open}" }
    let none = owned_type("void")
    cx
        .refused
        .push(
            Refused {
                at: e,
                want: none,
                found: none,
                seat: Seating
                    .LiteralUnpinned(lit.name.of, param, [spelled(t) for t in written], unwritten),
            },
        )
}

/// The record a literal names, applied to the type arguments it writes (`Box<int> { … }`), absent for
/// a literal that writes none, or not one for each of the record's parameters.
fn pinned_by(cx: Checking, e: ExprId, named: SignedType, params: int) -> SignedType? {
    let pinned = cx.store.struct_targs_of(e)
    if pinned.is_empty() || pinned.length != params { return null }
    named with { args: [cx.written(t) for t in pinned] }
}

Design for `impl_param_bound`, which the lead asked for before any build:

<to_controller>DESIGN impl_param_bound (`impl Respond for Created<T: Shown>`); no build until you say go:
1. Grammar. The impl head's target-argument list takes `type ( ":" bound:type )?` per argument (a new `impl_arg` rule used only inside `Name<…>`), so `T: Shown` and `List<int>` both read. No new statement branch, so no shared-leading-terminal risk; the FIRST-set check still runs on gen-2. A bound on a non-parameter argument (`List<int: X>`) is refused.
2. Storage. The bounds ride a side column like `struct_targs`, no `ImplDecl` shape change. The formatter prints them.
3. Signing. item_methods' `target_bounds` today reads the TYPE's declared bounds when the impl writes none; the impl's own written bounds take that slot (impl first, then type). They then reach every method's `FnSignature.bounds`.
4. Body: yes, a bare impl's body (`impl Created<T: Shown> { … }`) sees `T`'s trait methods, through the same `Signing.bound_of` a free fn's body uses. So `self.value.shown()` types, and an unbounded `T` still refuses "has no known methods".
5. Calls. A method call holds the impl's bound on the receiver's argument, via the `bounds_held` door `applied` already runs (`Created { value: "s" }.response()` → "`string` does not implement `Shown`"). Lowering keys a bounded parameter's unit by its fill, as a fn's are.
6. Old path: NewOnly.ImplBound (it refuses the form). The subset line "`impl T<K: Tr, V>` is expected `{`" and its case go in the same change.
7. Protocol: build/avra saved aside, gen-1 then gen-2, the whole tree re-read under the old vs new compiler (as for `b.m<T>`), witnesses red/green.

    for j, pp in parts.params {

    }

export fn unfed_lambda(mut cx: TypeCx, e: ExprId, seat: TypeId?) {
    if cx.facts.spoke_unfed(e) { return }
    cx.facts.mark_unfed(e)

    if cx.view.store.written_as_block(e) { return block_at_scalar(cx, e, at) }

<to_controller>DESIGN impl_param_bound (`impl Respond for Created<T: Shown>`); no build until you say go:
1. Grammar. The impl head's target-argument list takes `type ( ":" bound:type )?` per argument (a new `impl_arg` rule used only inside `Name<…>`), so `T: Shown` and `List<int>` both read. No new statement branch, so no shared-leading-terminal risk; the FIRST-set check still runs on gen-2. A bound on a non-parameter argument (`List<int: X>`) is refused.
2. Storage. The bounds ride a side column like `struct_targs`, no `ImplDecl` shape change. The formatter prints them.
3. Signing. item_methods' `target_bounds` today reads the TYPE's declared bounds when the impl writes none; the impl's own written bounds take that slot (impl first, then type). They then reach every method's `FnSignature.bounds`.
4. Body: yes, a bare impl's body (`impl Created<T: Shown> { … }`) sees `T`'s trait methods, through the same `Signing.bound_of` a free fn's body uses. So `self.value.shown()` types, and an unbounded `T` still refuses "has no known methods".

//! Parse-time lowering: a method call writing type arguments after its name, the arguments marked
//! on the call as a literal's are.
use core.{Built, Expr, Plain, Slots, computed}

/// `x.m<T>(a)` — the call, its written type arguments kept beside it in the store.
@computed
fn method_pinned_written(s: dyn Slots) -> Result<Built, string> {
    let store = s.arena()
    let call = store
        .alloc_expr(
            Expr.MethodCall(s.expr_of("subject")?, Plain(s.text_of("name")?), s.exprs_of("args")?),
            s.built_at(),
        )
    store.mark_struct_targs(call, s.types_of("pins")?)
    .Ok(Built.Expr(call))
}

    grammar: a method call writes its own type arguments after its name, `b.m<T>(a)`

//! Parse-time lowering: an impl whose target's arguments may each write a bound after a colon
//! (`impl Respond for Created<T: Shown>`), the bounds kept beside the statement in the store.
use core.{Built, Stmt, TypeRef, Nominal, Slots, computed}

/// `impl Tr for G<T: B> { … }` — the impl, its target's arguments as written and each one's bound
/// kept in the store's column for them. A bound stands on a type parameter alone: an argument
/// written as an applied, optional, `dyn` or fn type takes none.
@computed
fn impl_written(s: dyn Slots) -> Result<Built, string> {
    let store = s.arena()
    let args = s.params_of("target_args")?
    if args.any((a) -> a.bound != null && !bare(a.ty)) { return .Err(bound_on_type()) }
    let made = store
        .alloc_stmt(
            Stmt
                .ImplDecl(
                    [Nominal(t) for t in s.texts_of("of")?].first(),
                    s.types_of("of_args")?,
                    Nominal(s.text_of("target")?),
                    [a.ty! for a in args],
                    s.stmts_of("fns")?,
                ),
            s.built_at(),
        )
    let bounds: List<TypeRef?> = [a.bound for a in args]
    if bounds.any(it != null) { store.mark_impl_bounds(made, bounds) }
    .Ok(Built.Stmt(made))
}

/// Whether a written type is a bare name, as a type parameter is written.
fn bare(ty: TypeRef?) -> bool {
    let t? = ty else { return false }
    t.applied.is_empty() && !t.optional && !t.dynamic && !t.arrow && t.alternatives.is_empty()
}

fn bound_on_type() -> string { "a bound stands on a type parameter of the impl — `G<T: Bound>`, never on a written type" }
EOF

/// impl so bounded answers only for the types it accepts. A bound not known to fail holds.
fn bounds_met_by(engine: QueryEngine, reader: string, at: ImplAt, ty: SignedType) -> bool {
    let written = written_bounds(engine, at)
    if written.all(it == null) { return true }
    let signing = Signing { engine: engine, file: at.file, type_params: at.params }
    mut found: Map<string, SignedType> = Map.new()
    for j, a in ty.args { found.set("${j}", a) }
    for j, b in written {
        if b == null || j >= ty.args.length { continue }
        if implements(engine, reader, ty.args[j], signing.signed(b!).filled(found)) == false { return false }
    }
    true
}

### 2026-11-20T13:36:52 AGENT
The P0 fix failed one gate test on its first full run. The failure was a separate bug in the program layer that the fix exposed, and I've fixed that too. The full receipts are running again on both fixes together.

<to_controller>
P0, gen-2 receipts, first run:
- Green: make try, layer check, cli 0 refusals, gates a/b/d/e/f/g, witness 1039/1073 with 0 failing, idioms 0.
- Gate avrac-c FAIL, one new test: features/impls trait_bounds "an answer of `Self` is the implementing type's own".

Cause: a bug in the layer that predates the P0 change, now exposed by it.
- `applied_trait_fn` (item_methods.av) signs a trait fn with `Self` as the receiver, then fills the trait's own parameters with `.bound(args)`.
- A receiver that is the caller's own parameter `R` is `Parameter(0)`, the same place as the trait's first parameter `X`. So `r.remade(4)` in `fn f<R: Remade<int>>(r: R) -> R` typed as `int`.
- The body was never judged before the P0 fix, so this went unseen. `let x: R = r.remade(5)` was already refused at e3810d33.

Fix:
- `Self` is signed at a place past the trait's own parameters, `Parameter(n, "Self")`.
- It is then bound together with them: `args + [receiver]`. The static path goes through the same function, so it's fixed too.
- New witness builds_bound_self_answer: red on build/avra.pre-p0 ("`x` declares `R`, this is `int`"), green now, prints `4 5`.
- generic_answer_concrete, generic_return_concrete and builds_generic_answer_own all still hold.

Full gen-2 receipts are rerunning on both fixes. The squashed commit and bundle follow when green.
</to_controller>

```
# every store under the packages named emptied — a nested package's and a program test's too — so the
# rows after read them cold
cold() { for p in "$@"; do find "packages/$p" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \; ; done; return 0; }

# build/avra as HEAD's compiler: kept when it was built from this tree's compiler source, else made in
# ONE generation — from the committed seed's link where no compiler stands, else from the one that does
# — with the package libraries beside it, built without building the compiler again. A gate's
# compiler makes no claim of the net, so it is built without it; the two-generation fixed point is the
# build slice's.
compiler() {
    if compiler_stands; then return 0; fi
    if [ ! -x build/avra ]; then row compiler-recover make recover || return 1; fi
    row compiler-gen1 env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make avra || return 1
    row compiler-libs env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make -o avra libs
}

# what `$1`'s cold build of packages/cli took, in seconds, net on or off by `$2`
cli_built() {

// Builders render to S-expressions so every outcome is a plain string.

fn fold_render(v: Captured<Token, string>) -> string {
    match v {
        .Terminal(t) -> t.text,
        .Node(n) -> n,
        .Many(items) -> "[${joined([fold_render(x) for x in items], " ")}]",
        .Absent -> "_",
    }
}

/// `(name args)`, each argument rendered; a build's own name `at` also
/// answers where it was said to begin and end.
fn fold_build(name: string, args: List<Captured<Token, string>>, loc: Loc?) -> Result<
    Captured<Token, string>,
    string,
> {
    if name == "boom" { return Result.Err("boom") }
    mut out = "(${name}"
    for a in args { out = "${out} ${fold_render(a)}" }
    let at = if name.starts_with("at_") && loc != null { " @${loc!.lo}..${loc!.hi}" } else { "" }
    let built: Captured<Token, string> = Captured.Node("${out}${at})")
    Result.Ok(built)
}

        ready(g, avra_known_terminals()),
        lex_source(src).tokens,
        avra_lexeme(),
        fold_build,
    )
}

I've made `stands_in` compare types structurally instead of by spelling, and restarted the final receipts and cost run. One thing to flag: I kept the spelling comparison as a fallback for when the structures differ, rather than removing it outright.

<to_controller>
**`stands_in` change.** I stopped the final run while it was still on its first build.

The layer's `SignedType` has no id of its own. What the memo interner keys on is `quick_hash` plus `same_type`, a structural part-for-part equality, so `same_type` is the interned identity. `stands_as` (which `stands_in` → `reaches` asks) now does:
1. `self.same_type(seat)` first, so a type standing as itself spells nothing;
2. the spelling compare only when the structures differ, and the same for the `joined_with` path.

**Why I kept the spelling as a fallback.** Spelling is looser than structure. Two `Declared` types with the same name from different files spell the same but aren't the same type. Dropping the spelling test outright would change what's accepted in that case. That would arguably be a soundness fix, but it's a change of law. So I kept the fallback, and it only costs on the mismatch path.

Your call whether to drop it in a separate commit, with a witness for the same-name, different-file case.

1. fmt check
2. gen-1, then gen-2
3. full receipts: make try, layer check, cli, gates a..g, the full witness run, idioms
4. cost slice on the gen-2 builder

**Fix:** `seat_marks` folds all six marks, so `same_type` agrees with spelling on seats and the interner keeps them apart.
